A6_S5_D1: ^Young Noelle: Father, why are humans the ones who are able to build ships?
^Father: Part of it is coincidence, that we happened to live on an island with wood that fits boatmaking.
^Father: While the other is nature’s design.
^Narrator: You blinked up in confusion, ten and wide-eyed. Your father chuckles, showing you the various notebooks on his desk.
^Father: You see, we happen to have hands, which allow us to hold and make tools easier than other beings. It also helps us to write, which is why we have so many books.
^Father: But know this, Noelle. When you face something that feels too big to bear, just remember —
^Father: Nature’s design is only half of the work. The other half, is up to you.
